page: Google Cloud Platform n4a-highmem-2 is a virtual machine configuration built on the arm64 architecture. The instance provides 2 dedicated virtual CPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory, resulting in an allocation of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware accelerators are not present, and the instance includes no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent disk operations.

The 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides significant memory capacity relative to compute resources. Utilizing dedicated arm64 processor cores delivers consistent execution predictability for lightweight processing requirements. In terms of resource allocation, the high memory density per core offers qualitative cost efficiency for applications that would otherwise require provisioning excess compute capacity simply to acquire sufficient RAM.

Without integrated local disks or specialized accelerators, the instance is geared toward compute tasks that interface with external databases or decoupled storage. Google Cloud Platform n4a-highmem-2 is well aligned with memory-intensive workloads that require limited processing power, including in-memory key-value caching layers, lightweight relational databases, microservices, and staging platforms.

Google Cloud Platform n4a-highmem-2 is technically structured for memory-heavy services with moderate processing requirements, including distributed cache nodes, lightweight relational database instances, background message workers, and application backends requiring elevated memory headroom.
